data.description:
Build the sponsor-contact portal designed and loved 2026-08-14. Binding design contract: prototypes/sponsor-portal/index.html (commit 6ab0b7ee) reproduced one-to-one, plus sequence/sponsors-design.md §3.3 and §5 (the round's rulings). Flight Deck rules bind as everywhere; judge's vocabulary is law (Session, Portal, Task).

WHAT IT IS — the speaker portal's sibling: magic-link entry (existing auth), public-shell chrome, SPEC §3.7 task machinery. Center of gravity is the SPONSORSHIP. Page order: head (welcome + N-of-M deliverables meter) → sponsorship hero (company · tier chip · status · derived deal line read from attached data — Sessions count, booth number, passes — never a tier blurb; organizer contact on the right) → booth location card (speaker location-card machinery reused: loc-lines, load-in leave-by box, venue map; rendered only when booth data exists, absence ordinary) → deliverables (task rows with assignee labeling, overdue markers, cancelled-block with reason once) → Sessions cards (read-only) → company profile (org-level, contact roster, Primary/You chips) → sponsor handbook.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (stable AC IDs minted at consolidation):
1. A sponsorship_contact enters by magic link and sees the whole sponsorship: every deliverable with its assignee named ("yours" / "assigned to X").
2. ANY signed-in contact can complete ANY open deliverable; completion records and displays attribution ("completed by <name>"), including when completer ≠ assignee. Chase board reflects immediately.
3. Task kinds render their real payloads (acknowledge / file request / form) with kind-specific validation; cancelled tasks sit below a dashed divider, reason stated once, excluded from progress; completed work is never restyled by cancellation (SPEC §3.7 semantics).
4. Sessions are read-only cards; the task machinery is the single write path ("Name your speaker" completion fills the Session's speaker; "Session title/description" tasks fill content). Honest empties: "Speaker not named yet" links to its task; unscheduled states when scheduling happens; unpublished slots carry "Not yet public".
5. A booth-bearing sponsorship renders the booth card (number, hall, building, load-in window, access note, leave-by line, map); a boothless one simply composes down — no special casing either way (ruling 5).
6. Derived deal line in hero: chips computed from linked Sessions, booth data, passes. Nothing hardcoded per tier — the portal shows the deliverables it is given (tier-scoped content variation is a Later band).
7. Company profile edits write org-level company facts; contacts are read-only in the portal (managed by the organizer), Primary and You marked.
8. Seed/demo data carries BOTH prototype views (operator ruling 2026-08-14: keep the prototype views in the build): a Gold booth-bearing sponsorship with 3 contacts, an overdue task, a cancelled task, one scheduled + one speakerless Session; and a Silver boothless single-contact sponsorship. Both demonstrable end-to-end.
9. Craft: elements never jump (fixed-width task action buttons, reserved states), tabular numerals, honest empty/loading/error states, R7 speed.

DEPENDENCY: requires the sponsors-module data layer (sequence/sponsors-design.md §3.1: companies, sponsor_tiers, sponsorships, sponsorship_contacts, task-join for grouping, nullable sponsorship_id on submissions) and organizer-side surfaces — NOT YET TICKETED. This ticket should be linked blocked_by that ticket when it is minted. Contract-time work: tone-architect to spec the attribution field (completed-by actor on task completion) as a SPEC amendment.

OPERATOR HOLD (Atin, 2026-08-14): do not start a worker on this ticket yet — machine overloaded. Design and cut only.
data.title: Sponsor portal: sponsor-contact portal on the speaker-portal machinery

data.body: Operator hold LIFTED (Atin, 2026-08-14, later the same day): build authorized. Delegator agent:mrq-214-opus launched on Claude Opus at high effort — surface:381, worktree ../Marquee-worktrees/mrq-214-sponsor-portal cut from github/main @2f659904. Scope ruling delivered in its boot prompt: minimal sponsors data layer IN scope, organizer-side sponsor screens OUT. The description's hold paragraph is superseded by this comment.

Claimed by agent:mrq-214-opus (Claude Opus, high effort; operator-authorized launch 2026-08-14).

SCOPE RULING from parent (sponsor-portal design surface), recorded here so it is durable:

IN scope for MRQ-214 — the minimal sponsors data layer the portal needs:
- migrations + API for companies, sponsor_tiers, sponsorships, sponsorship_contacts
- the deliverables join (person-assigned speaker_tasks grouped by sponsorship)
- sponsor-contact magic-link entry
- seed data carrying BOTH prototype views (AC 8)
- the completed-by attribution field on task completion (SPEC amendment)

OUT of scope — its own ticket later:
- organizer-side Sponsors list, sponsorship record, tier settings, chase integration, CRM companies facet

Rationale: a portal with no data is a dead end; a portal build that swallows the whole module is scope creep. The dependency the ticket names is therefore satisfied in-ticket at the minimum viable width, not deferred.

Data doctrine held: contacts are people rows (never a parallel table); no workflow status on people; booth is sponsorship data, not a record type; tier-scoped portal CONTENT variation stays a Later band — the portal renders the deliverables it is given.

Plan written (.lattice/plans/task_01M012DRCPFPZH6MRP0JZ0YWRY.md) → planned → in_progress.

Shape of the build, in the order it will be committed:
1. migrations/0022_sponsors.sql — companies, sponsor_tiers, sponsorships, sponsorship_contacts; people.company_id; speaker_tasks.sponsorship_id + completed_by_person_id (the attribution field); submissions.sponsorship_id. Schema mirror (src/db/schema.ts) and schema-verify move 53 -> 57 tables.
2. Seed module scripts/seed/sponsors.ts — Gold booth-bearing (3 contacts incl. a diacritic name, overdue task, cancelled task with reason, one scheduled + one speakerless Session) and Silver boothless single-contact.
3. API — GET /api/v1/me/sponsor-portal, PATCH /api/v1/me/sponsorships/{id}/company, and two WIDENED existing predicates so the task machinery stays the single write path: POST /me/tasks/{id}/complete and POST /me/uploads/sign both accept a sponsorship contact acting on a colleague's task, through one shared predicate in src/lib/sponsors/task-access.ts. Speaker resolution untouched.
4. Entry — ROLE_HOME.sponsor = /sponsor-portal; roleHome() returns it only when the person holds no staff/reviewer/speaker role, so every existing answer is unchanged. No new demo door: DEMO_ROLE_TO_MEMBERSHIP maps to a membership role and a sponsorship contact is not one. Seeded contacts are is_demo=1, so the on-screen magic link is the demo path.
5. UI — SponsorPortalPage.tsx reproducing the prototype one-to-one, with the speaker portal's task machinery EXTRACTED to src/ui/portal/task-machinery.tsx rather than copied (TaskRow gains optional assignee/attribution props the speaker portal does not pass).
6. SPEC Amendment 23 (attribution field, sponsors tables, new §5.14). No AC IDs minted; tests/ac-claims/MRQ-214.json declares owns: [].

Two scope decisions recorded so the later organizer-side ticket is not surprised: no task_templates.sponsor_tier_id (tier template sets belong to the surface that authors them; half a reconciliation is worse than none) and no companies.logo_attachment_id (the logo arrives as a file deliverable; the column lands with the surface that needs it).

Also noticed while reading: SPEC.md carries Amendment 22 duplicated verbatim at its tail. Removing one copy as tidiness, called out in the PR body.

Build complete through the UI; tests and validation next.

Committed so far: data layer -> seed + write-back -> API + entry -> extraction + seed invariants -> the page.

TWO THINGS THE OPERATOR/PARENT SHOULD KNOW:

1. **check:routes has been failing on main**, since route-table.ts grew its first relative import (MRQ-209's org-home). Node's type stripping resolves extensionless relative specifiers literally, so the script's import of route-table.ts dies with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND and the gate — and therefore pr-gate, which includes it — has been red for every agent. Verified failing at the branch base 2f659904 in a scratch worktree before touching anything. Fixed in this branch inside check-routes.mjs (a resolve hook), because extensions cannot go in the source: tsconfig.client.json has allowImportingTsExtensions off, so the browser build rejects them. If a sibling agent has been re-running pr-gate and blaming their own diff, this is why.

2. **Two acknowledged divergences from the prototype**, both deliberate consistency calls, both to be named in the PR body:
   - The prototype opens tasks and handbook pages in MODALS. The shipped speaker portal expands task rows in place, and the ticket says 'exact task-row machinery'. So both portals expand in place, and the handbook chapters do too. Choosing the prototype's modal here would have meant a second task-completion UI in the same product.
   - The prototype's dashed 'Prototype' switcher is prototype chrome and does not ship. A REAL sponsorship switcher renders in its place, and only when the signed-in contact genuinely holds more than one deal.

Also worth recording: naming a speaker through the deliverable now calls reconcileTaskSet, the same idempotent reconciliation the acceptance boundary runs. A seed test caught that a named sponsor speaker was getting a membership without the onboarding task set SPEC §6 says every accepted speaker carries — the same gap existed at runtime, so it was fixed in both places rather than only where the test could see it.

VALIDATION PASSED — driven in the c11 embedded browser against the BUILT Worker (wrangler dev on the dist bundle, INSECURE_LOCAL_COOKIES=1), not vite dev. Evidence attached (artifacts/mrq-214/validation.md plus both views' full rendered page text).

Eight steps, all pass:
1. Magic link for dana.okafor@example.com -> 302 Location: /sponsor-portal, cookie without Secure. This is the whole point of the entry work: before it, the same link landed a contact on the speaker portal's honest 'you have no speaker record'.
2. Gold view complete: derived deal line '2 Sessions · Booth 214 · 6 conference passes', organizer contact read from a real staff membership, booth card with map and leave-by, eight deliverables each naming its assignee, '1 OVERDUE' chip, cancelled block with its reason stated once, honest Session empties, 3 handbook chapters.
3. ANYONE-COMPLETES WITH ATTRIBUTION, through the UI: signed in as Dana, completed the deliverable ASSIGNED TO PRIYA. Row now reads 'completed by Dana Okafor' with the assignee unchanged; meter 3 of 7 -> 4 of 7.
4. NAME YOUR SPEAKER: the Session card's link jumped to and opened the deliverable (#deliverable-<id>); completing it filled the Session with 'Íde Ní Chonaráin-Okwuosa' and the action swapped to the honest scheduling sentence. The database shows a real seat: 1 speaker membership, 1 participation, and 2 onboarding tasks — the deliverable's promise is literally true.
5. Upload signer (curl, since the webview has no file picker): Dana presigning GRZEGORZ's deliverable -> 200; Mona, a contact of the other deal -> 403.
6. Company profile edit persisted across a reload and on the companies row — org level, as the editor says.
7. Silver view composes down: NO booth card, no booth chip, one contact, 'NOT YET PUBLIC' on the scheduled Session, and only 2 handbook chapters (no load-in guide).
8. Console clean throughout; no layout jump on any action.

Two seed corrections that only driving the real artifact would have surfaced, both committed:
- the overdue deliverable was 5 days behind the seed's FROZEN clock while 'overdue' derives against the REAL one, so the one state that row exists to show was not on screen before the frozen date. Now 12 days back, past both.
- Silver's Session had nobody named and no deliverable that could name them. Yusuf Demirtaş now speaks it, so 'Speaker not named yet' appears only where the deliverable exists to fix it.

Could not capture: c11 browser screenshot fails with internal_error on this build INCLUDING on /health, so it is not this page. Page text plus database reads stand in, and they are checkable rather than merely visual.

PR OPEN: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/274

INDEPENDENT REVIEW DONE AND CLOSED. A clear Claude reviewer read the diff with no context from me (artifacts/mrq-214/review.md, 329 lines). It found TWO BLOCKING defects and both were real:

1. Event deletion would have 500'd the moment a sponsor existed. deleteEventCascade hand-enumerates every event-owned table into one D1 batch and had never been taught these four tables. That does not fail loudly — it makes the conference UNDELETABLE and takes POST /admin/remove-demo with it, on the very event the seed puts sponsors on. Fixed; two integration tests now delete a conference holding a sponsorship, and I proved the test bites by reverting the fix and watching it fail with FOREIGN KEY constraint failed.

2. A cross-tenant leak. organizerContactFor bound only eventId, so an org-wide owner/program_lead/ops membership in ANY organization was an eligible candidate — and that name and address are printed on the page and in the handbook FAQ. Now organization-scoped, with this conference's own staff sorting ahead of the organization's general staff.

Also closed from the same review: the write-back now proves the task's two independent joins agree; sponsorships.tier_id becomes a composite FK like the building beside it (a single-column FK let another conference's tier attach and the failure was SILENT — the portal joins on event_id, so a mis-scoped tier rendered as no tier); the overdue chip is always rendered so completing the last overdue item stops sliding the count beside it; chips lose their uppercase; three seed assertions that were genuinely weaker rather than sharper are tightened; boothFor now counts all seven booth columns; one tier name per conference. The declared prototype-divergence list went from three to six, because the real one was longer than the declared one.

The review's CLEARED section is worth reading too: it independently traced the shared authorization predicate across cross-org, cross-conference, cross-sponsorship, cancelled-task, api-token and co-speaker-roleHint angles and found it sound, and confirmed line-by-line that the speaker portal's read and completion paths are behaviourally unchanged by the extraction and by the UPDATE's scoping change.

GATE: pr-gate pass-over-budget (every check passed; slow on a shared box). npm test 203 files / 1434 tests / 0 failures. schema, seed, design, api, routes, clocks, shell-truth, trace:ac all pass.

One thing for whoever reads this next: check:routes had been DARK on main since MRQ-209's route-table import — Node type stripping resolves extensionless relative specifiers literally, so the script's import died and pr-gate went red for the whole fleet. Verified failing at the branch base AND at github/main in a scratch worktree before touching it. Fixed in this branch. If a sibling agent has been re-running pr-gate and blaming their own diff, that is why.

Next: merge on green + this review, per CLAUDE.md. Merging does not deploy and I am not deploying.

MERGED as 1cce684a (PR #274, squash). CI fast-gate green; board home fast-forwarded to the merge commit and the working copy verified (sponsor-portal.routes.ts, migrations/0023_sponsors.sql, SPEC Amendment 23 all present).

WHAT SHIPPED
The sponsor portal at /sponsor-portal, reproducing the loved prototype: head with an N-of-M deliverables meter, sponsorship hero with a DERIVED deal line, booth card when there is a booth, deliverables with per-row assignee and attribution, read-only Session cards, org-level company profile with the contact roster, and a sponsor handbook whose load-in chapter appears only for a sponsorship that has a booth.

Plus the minimal data layer it needed to be a page rather than a mock: companies (org-scoped), sponsor_tiers and sponsorships (event-scoped, booth as columns), sponsorship_contacts, the deliverables join on speaker_tasks, the Sessions join on submissions, and speaker_tasks.completed_by_person_id — the attribution field the ticket anticipated, now SPEC Amendment 23.

THE THREE RULINGS, MADE LITERAL
- Whole sponsorship, anyone completes, attribution recorded. Proven in a browser: signed in as Dana, completed the deliverable assigned to Priya, and the row reads 'completed by Dana Okafor' with the assignee unchanged.
- The hero is the sponsorship, and its deal line is computed from what is attached — never a per-tier blurb.
- Sessions are read-only; the task machinery is the single write path. Completing 'Name your speaker' creates the person, the participation, and — through the same reconcileTaskSet the acceptance boundary runs — their membership and onboarding task set, so the promise printed on the task is literally true (verified: 1 membership, 1 participation, 2 tasks).

KEY DECISIONS a later ticket inherits
- Two routes added; TWO WIDENED, not duplicated: /me/tasks/{id}/complete and /me/uploads/sign both resolve through the speaker predicate OR the sponsorship-contact predicate from ONE shared function, because two near-identical predicates would give a contact a file deliverable that opens, validates, then fails at the PUT.
- The task projection and the whole task-row UI are EXTRACTED (portal-tasks.queries.ts, task-machinery.tsx), not copied.
- The completion UPDATE is scoped to the task's assignee rather than the caller — inert for a speaker, the point for a sponsor.
- No task_templates.sponsor_tier_id and no companies.logo_attachment_id: tier template sets and logo uploads belong to the organizer surface that authors them.
- No unique constraint on companies(org_id, name): right shape, but a hard constraint without a merge affordance turns a rename into an error the organizer cannot resolve.

FOUR DEFECTS FOUND RATHER THAN SHIPPED
1. (review, BLOCKING) Event deletion would have 500'd the moment a sponsor existed — deleteEventCascade had never been taught these tables, which does not fail loudly but makes the conference UNDELETABLE and takes remove-demo with it. Fixed; two integration tests now delete a conference holding a sponsorship, and I proved the test bites by reverting the fix and watching FOREIGN KEY constraint failed.
2. (review, BLOCKING) Cross-tenant leak: organizerContactFor bound only eventId, so an org-wide staff membership in ANY organization could be printed on the page and in the handbook as 'your organizer'. Now organization-scoped.
3. (tests) A deliverable's accept list was a lie — 'vector (SVG or EPS)' against an upload policy that sniffs pdf/pptx/key only. Now states what the product can take. Widening the sniffer is a security-surface change and was NOT quietly done.
4. (seed test, then runtime) A named sponsor speaker was getting a seat with an empty portal. Fixed in both places.

Also closed from the review: write-back join agreement, a composite tier FK (a single-column FK let another conference's tier attach and the failure was SILENT), a chip that slid its sibling when the last overdue item was completed, chip casing, three seed assertions that were weaker rather than sharper, boothFor counting three of seven booth columns, and one-tier-name-per-conference.

TWO THINGS FOR THE FLEET
- check:routes had been DARK on main since MRQ-209's route-table import (Node type stripping resolves extensionless relative specifiers literally), so pr-gate was red for every agent. Verified failing at the branch base AND at github/main before touching it; fixed in this PR.
- The primary checkout carried a STALE .git/index.lock, zero bytes, timestamped 17:40 — a crashed process's leftover that was blocking every index operation in the board home for the whole fleet. No live git process existed; removed it (git's own instruction for exactly this), fast-forwarded, and left every .lattice working-tree change alone.

GATE: pr-gate pass-over-budget (every check passed); npm test 203 files / 1434 tests / 0 failures; schema, seed, design, api, routes, clocks, shell-truth, trace:ac all pass. Adopted main's new migration-delta schema verification (scripts/schema-deltas/0023_sponsors.json: 4 tables, 14 FK rows).

Validation evidence: artifacts/mrq-214/validation.md; independent review: artifacts/mrq-214/review.md. Merging does not deploy, and nothing here was deployed.
